steps: Remove the top plate and confirm the integrated certified safety-barrier screens on the front door and side glass are in place — they must stay installed. Review all requirements first.

Rear 1½", sides 10", corner 5⅝", ceiling 43". Approved directly on combustible floors — no hearth pad required — but never on thick carpet or foam, which lets the stove settle and can leak the vent. Alcove min 44"W × 24"D × 60"H.
Ships for natural gas. For propane, convert with kit 158329 — swap to the #52 burner orifice and the .013" LP pilot injector, and fit the LP regulator tower. Authorized technician only.

Vertical or horizontal coaxial (4" inner / 6⅝" outer). Use one approved brand only — DuraVent DirectVent Pro and listed equivalents — never mixed. Seal the inner pipe with a 1/8" bead of high-temp cement (no silicone). Horizontal: ≤30 ft vertical and ≤20 ft horizontal, with a 12" rise and 6" run minimum. Set the exhaust restrictor plate per the vent matrix.

3/8" NPT supply (about 12" off the rear centerline) with a manual shut-off (T-handle in MA) and union in the same room. Leak-test every joint. Verify inlet and manifold pressure with the knob on HIGH at the A (manifold) and B (inlet) ports.
Install the Beach Fire log set and rock-wool embers; add the optional reflective or fluted liner and ash lip if used. Wear gloves and keep embers clear of the pilot.

Provide a grounded outlet within 6 ft of the vent centerline. Fit the optional blower kit; wire a 750 mV remote or thermostat to the terminal block right of the valve. Set the rear switch to T-STAT for thermostatic or remote control.

Purge the line on first light and, from cold, let the pilot burn 10–15 minutes to build draft before the burner. The pilot should engulf the top 1/8" of the thermocouple and thermopile. Tune the air shutter (factory NG 1/16", LP 1/8") for a clean flame with no soot.

panels.title: Insufficient pressure
items: Small pilot flame → weak millivolt signal and burner outages
Little change in flame between HI and LO on the regulator knob
Undersized supply feeding several appliances → nuisance dropouts or surges

items: Permanent valve damage → full appliance shutdown
Oversized pilot flame overheats the sensor → shutdown
Sooting and white residue from flame impingement / wrong fuel-air mix

light.title: Lighting the stove
light.html:
Before lighting, smell all around the stove for gas, including near the floor. If you smell gas, stop — see Safety & gas smell.

Both versions of the GF 520 — the DV and the DV MV — have a standing pilot that you light by hand with the red igniter button.

  1. Set the BURNER ON/OFF switch to OFF.
  2. Confirm the gas supply shut-off valve is open.
  3. Push the control knob in slightly and turn it clockwise to OFF. Wait 5 minutes — still smell gas? Stop.
  4. Turn the knob counter-clockwise to PILOT, push it all the way in and hold.
  5. Press the red igniter button repeatedly until the pilot lights; keep holding about one minute, then release. It should stay lit.
  6. Turn the knob to ON, then set the BURNER switch to ON.
Use only your hand to push in or turn the gas control knob. Never use tools. If the knob won't push in or turn by hand, don't try to repair it. Call a qualified technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.
Don't use the stove if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect it and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.
DV MV pilot timer: on the DV MV, the pilot shuts off on its own after 7 days with no call for heat — re-light it with the same steps. From a cold start, let the pilot burn 10–15 minutes to build draft before running the burner.
Note: the manual describes pilot lighting two ways. One paragraph on p. 35 says the stove has an ignition device that lights the pilot automatically, and not to light the pilot by hand. The lighting instructions (p. 47, also printed on the rating plate), the pilot parts (p. 32) and the parts list with its piezo igniter (p. 42) all describe a hand-lit pilot. These steps follow the lighting instructions, as p. 35 also says to do.

flame.title: Adjusting the flame & heat
flame.html:
Set flame height and heat with the regulator knob in the controls compartment. The rear rocker switch handles ON/OFF, or T-STAT for thermostat / remote control.

Pilot and air-shutter adjustments are a qualified technician's job — not a homeowner setting.

Long yellow flames, soot, or heavy white residue point to a fuel-air problem — clean the glass (see below) and have the air shutter checked.

remote.title: Remote & thermostat
remote.html:
The stove accepts an optional 750 mV wall thermostat (750003) or a remote control (224910).

  1. Make sure the pilot is lit — it powers the control circuit.
  2. Set the rear rocker switch to T-STAT.
  3. Operate from the thermostat or remote per its own instructions.
On a thermostat or remote, the stove can fire on its own and stays very hot even when the burner looks off. Keep the remote where children can't reach it.

off.title: Turning it off
off.html:
Pause the flame

Set the rear rocker switch to OFF.

Turn off the pilot

Push the control knob in slightly and turn it clockwise to OFF (don't force it). On the DV MV, the pilot also times out on its own after 7 days unused.

Shut it down fully

Close the supply-line gas cock.

Use only your hand to push in or turn the gas control knob. Never use tools, and don't force it. If the knob won't push in or turn by hand, don't try to repair it. Call a qualified technician. Force or attempted repair may result in a fire or explosion.

pilot.title: Checking the pilot flame
pilot.html:
The pilot sits behind the burner at the rear of the firebox.

A healthy pilot is steady — not lifting or floating — blue around the hood with a little yellow at the edges, and reaches up to engulf the top 1/8" of the thermocouple and thermopile.

Weak or won't stay lit? That's a service call — pilot adjustment must be done by a qualified technician.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Never run the stove with any glass panel removed, cracked or broken; never clean the glass hot; and never use ammonia-based or abrasive cleaners.

After the first few fires a white powdery residue appears as the burner media cures. Clean it off promptly with a non-abrasive hearth gas-appliance glass cleaner and warm water — if left on, it can permanently etch the glass.

  1. Let the glass cool completely.
  2. Wipe with the cleaner or warm water on a soft cloth.
  3. Dry with a soft towel; don't scratch the surface.
The integrated safety-barrier screens must stay installed; replacement screens and glass come only from your Jøtul dealer.

blower.title: Running the blower
blower.html:
The optional blower kit (158333) circulates warm air off the firebox and into the room.

Once installed, it's driven by a heat-activated switch and has a speed control — it comes on after the stove warms up and shuts off as it cools.

Set-up and control details are in the blower kit instructions.

sounds.title: Odors, fog & the first few fires
sounds.html:
Odor and some smoke at first

The high-temperature paint heat-cures during the first fires, giving off odor and some visible smoke. Operate low for a few hours, then high for a few hours, with plenty of fresh air. It passes.

Fog and white residue on the glass

A little fog at each lighting is normal and clears as the glass warms. The white powdery film after early fires is curing residue — clean it off (see Clean the glass) before it etches.

A strong gas smell is different. Don't light anything or touch switches or phones inside — leave immediately and call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone. See Safety & gas smell.

safety.title: Safety & what to do if you smell gas
safety.html:
• The glass and surfaces get very hot — and stay hot after the burner looks off. Keep children and at-risk individuals away.
  • The integrated certified safety-barrier screens on the front door and side glass must remain installed at all times; if one is damaged, get the original-equipment replacement from your dealer.
  • Never store or use gasoline or flammable liquids near the stove.
  • Gas or propane only — never burn solid fuel.
  • Don't use the stove if any part has been under water. Immediately call a qualified service technician to inspect it and to replace any part of the control system and any gas control that has been under water.
If you smell gas: do NOT try to light anything. Put out any open flame. Open windows. Do NOT touch electrical switches or use a phone in the building. Leave the building immediately. Immediately call your gas supplier from a neighbor's phone, and follow the gas supplier's instructions. If you can't reach your gas supplier, call the fire department.
Massachusetts: a carbon-monoxide detector must be installed in the same room as the appliance.

service.title: Annual service & warranty
service.html:
Have the stove and its vent inspected and cleaned at least once a year by a qualified technician. Always shut off the gas before any service work.

Cast iron, firebox5 years
Burner, firebox panels2 years
Enamel finish2 years
Gas & electrical (valve, controls, blower)1 year
This is a summary. Full warranty terms and exclusions are in the official PDF.

specInput.title: Input rates & efficiency
specInput.html:
NG max / min30,000 / 16,500 BTU/hr
LP max / min29,000 / 16,500 BTU/hr

Steady-state efficiency 70.01% NG / 71.72% LP. CSA P4.1-15 fireplace efficiency: DV 61.47% NG / 62.15% LP · DV MV 63.49% NG / 64.61% LP.

specInlet.title: Inlet (supply) pressure
specInlet.html:
Natural gas5.0 – 7.0 in. WC
Propane12.0 – 14.0 in. WC
Note: the Specifications page (p. 4) lists the LP inlet minimum as 12.0 WC; the Gas Pressure section (p. 20) lists it as 11.0 WC.

Measure at the B (inlet) test port on the front of the valve with the control knob on HIGH. An external regulator is required for propane.

specManifold.title: Manifold pressure
specManifold.html:
Natural gas1.12 – 3.80 in. WC
Propane2.9 – 11.0 in. WC
Note: the Specifications page (p. 4) lists manifold pressure as 1.12 – 3.80 natural gas and 2.9 – 11.0 propane; the Gas Pressure section (p. 20) lists it as 1.6 – 3.5 natural gas and 6.4 – 10.0 propane (in. WC).

Measure at the A (manifold) test port, knob on HIGH. The pilot should be blue at the hood with yellow at the edges and engulf the top 1/8" of both the thermocouple and the thermopile.

specVent.title: Venting — direct vent
specVent.html:
Sealed direct-vent only. Use parts from one approved manufacturer — DuraVent DirectVent Pro / GS and listed equivalents — never mixed. Seal the inner pipe joints with a 1/8" bead of high-temp cement; do not use silicone.
Pipe4" inner / 6⅝" outer coaxial
Terminationvertical or horizontal
Horizontal: max vertical30 ft
Horizontal: max horizontal20 ft
Min. rise / run12" rise + 6" run

Slope horizontal runs 1/4" per foot up — never downward. Set the rear exhaust-restrictor plate per the vent-window matrix. Termination clearance: 3" to combustible projections ≤2½", 12" to projections over 2½". Wall cut-out 10" × 10". Co-linear termination allowed with a 2 ft max horizontal run.

specClear.title: Clearances & floor
specClear.html:
Rear (rear shroud)1½"
Side (side plate)10"
Corner (side plate)5⅝"
Ceiling (top plate)43"

Vent-pipe clearances: 1" on all sides of vertical runs; on horizontal runs 2" off the top and 1" off the sides and bottom. Alcove minimum 44"W × 24"D × 60"H.

Floor: approved directly on combustible floors — no floor protection required — but not on a compressible surface like thick carpet or foam, which lets the stove settle and can leak the vent.

specFuel.title: Fuel & orifices
specFuel.html:
NG burner orifice#37
LP burner orifice#52
Pilot injectorNG .020" / LP .013"
Air shutter (factory)NG 1/16" / LP 1/8"

Ships for natural gas. Convert to LP with kit 158329 (back to NG with 158330) — authorized technician only. Do not alter or modify components.
